sentences.text: THE HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE J.M.KHAZI
ORAL ORDER (PER: THE HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE J.M.KHAZI)

In this petition filed under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short, 'BNSS'), the petitioners who are arraigned as accused Nos.4 and 5 are seeking bail in Crime No.120/2024 of Gokak Rural Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 489A, 489B, 489C and 420 of IPC.
2.
In support of the petition, the petitioners have contended that they are innocent of the offences alleged and having valid and tenable defence.
There is no material to show that they are indulged in counterfeiting of currency notes or using counterfeit notes as genuine.
It is alleged that petitioners were found in possession of currency notes of Rs.100/- and Rs.500/- denominations of Children Bank of India.
The said allegation would not attract provisions of Sections 489A, 489B and 489C.
No independent role attributed to the petitioners.
Already NC: 2024:KHC-D:13089 accused No.10 is granted bail.
Petitioners are also standing on the same footing.
Major portion of the investigation is completed.
Petitioners are not involved in any other cases.
Petitioners are permanent residents of addresses given in the cause title.
They are ready and willing to abide by any conditions that may be imposed and offers substantial surety to the satisfaction of the trial Court and hence, the petition.

3. Learned HCGP submitted oral objections stating that on 28.6.2024 at 11.00 p.m., on receipt of credible information, the complainant intercepted a white car bearing registration No.KA-22/G-1075, coming from Fort Circle side Kadabagatti-Kanasageri Road near Sri Chowdeshwari Temple, accused Nos.1 to 5 were found in the said car.
A black bag containing notes of 100 and 500 denominations were found in the said car bearing the mark Children's Bank of India.
The accused persons disclosed that they would exchange these notes in the ratio of 4:1 per genuine currency.
Therefore, accused NC: 2024:KHC-D:13089 Nos.1 to 5 were arrested and the counterfeit notes found with them are seized.
Later, accused Nos.6 to 10 are arrested and remanded to custody.
From the possession of the accused persons, car bearing registration No.KA-38/M- 6049 and five bundles of blank papers of the size of 500 denomination currency notes and two cell phones are seized.
If petitioners are released on bail, there is likelihood of the petitioners indulging in similar offence and may also abscond and prays to reject the petition.

4. Heard the arguments and perused the records.
5.

According to the prosecution, on 28.6.2024 at 11.00 p.m., on receipt of credible information, the complainant along with his staff intercepted a white car bearing registration number KA-22/-G-1075, coming from Court Circle side on Kadabagatti-Kanasageri Road near Sri Chowdeshwari Temple.
Accused Nos.1 to 5 were found in the said car.

sentences.text: The accused persons NC: 2024:KHC-D:13089 disclosed that they would exchange these notes in the ratio of 4:1 per genuine currency.
Therefore, accused Nos.1 to 5 were arrested and the counterfeit notes found with them are seized.
Later, accused Nos.6 to 10 are arrested and remanded to custody.

From the possession of the said accused persons, car bearing registration number KA-38/M-6049 and five bundles of blank papers of the size of 500 denomination currency notes and two cell phones are seized.

6. As per the prosecution case, what is found in possession of the accused persons are certain notes containing the mark Children's Bank of India, which appears to be used for school projects by the students.
From the description of the seized articles, it appears to be the material required by the students for carrying on the school projects and also children used for playing.

Other than the allegations that the currency notes bearing the mark Children's Bank of India, no other articles were found which indicate that the accused persons are NC: 2024:KHC-D:13089 indulged in counterfeiting currency notes.
The allegations against the petitioners are that they were found in possession of five bundles of white paper of the measurement of 500 currency note.
They are produced before the trial Court with the application seeking judicial custody which indicates that no longer their custody is required for the purpose of investigation.
Of course, there is apprehension that the petitioners may abscond and also threaten or temper with the witnesses which may be overcome by imposing conditions.

In the above facts and circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that petitioners are entitled for bail and accordingly, the following:
ORDER Petition is allowed.

Petitioners/accused Nos.4 and 5 are released on bail in Crime No.120/2024 of Gokak Rural Police Station for the offence punishable under Sections 120B, 489A, 489B, 489C and 420 of IPC, subject to following:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:13089 CONDITIONS
a) The petitioners/accused Nos.4 and 5
shall execute a personal bond in a sum of 50,000/- each with one surety for the like- sum to the satisfaction of the trial Court.
b) They shall make themselves available for the purpose of investigation as and when required and they shall co-operate with the investigation.
c) They shall furnish their residential address proof and shall inform the Investigating Officer/Court, if there is any change in the address.
d) They shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses either directly or indirectly.
e) They shall not indulge in any criminal activities.
f) They shall be regular in attending the Court proceedings.
